title: observation-controller-for-gradual-rollouts-and-auto-rollback
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an observation controller that continuously evaluates quality regressions during progressive canary and A/B rollouts and triggers automated rollback policies when statistically significant regressions are detected. The controller must operate across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and integrate with Redwood Console dashboards, alerts, and rollout policy engine. Focus areas: 1) robust statistical testing (sequential/hypothesis test) to avoid noise-driven rollbacks, 2) cohort-aware evaluation with per-tenant baselines, 3) configurable risk budgets and burn-in periods, 4) clear automation actions (rollback, scale adjustments, notify), and 5) audit logs for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes per-metric p-values and effect sizes in streaming fashion for defined cohorts and traffic slices
Rollback is automatically executed when configured thresholds are breached for configured consecutive windows (default 3 windows) and risk budget remains
Rollbacks are idempotent and revert traffic to previously pinned model/config version with < 30s routing switch on Hosted deployments
All decisions logged to audit trail (Console + customer audit) with linked eval snapshots and PR references
Manual override via Console (pause/force-commit rollback) supported and surfaces reason + affected cohorts
Integration tests simulate A/B traffic with injected regressions and assert rollback triggers and notification emissions
SLO dashboard shows pre/post-rollout quality metrics and indicates rollback events for 90 days
Rollout policy respects Dedicated and Private deployment constraints (no cross-customer automatic rollback unless tenant-specific)
Performance: observation controller adds <5% CPU overhead on control-plane instances at typical rollout scales
progress_updates: 2026-02-25 - Ticket created after spike in false-negatives during last canary; design brainstorm with SRE and PM done.
2026-02-28 - Prototype statistical engine implemented (sequential two-sided t-test + nonparametric fallback) and validated on historic eval runs; PR #7321 opened.
2026-03-02 - Decided to use risk-budget model (burn-rate) instead of single threshold to reduce noisy rollbacks; added cohort baselining to design.
2026-03-04 - Integration point with rollout policy engine defined: controller emits decisions to rollout-controller endpoint and includes confidence metadata.

2026-03-07 - Working POC deployed to staging; tested with synthetic A/B traffic. Found edge-case: small-cohort variance causes over-sensitive p-values — added minimum sample-size guard and Bayesian smoothing.
Next: harden alerts, add audit export, write end-to-end tests, and prepare docs for Console integration.
tech_notes: Statistical approach: sequential hypothesis tests with alpha spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) to keep overall false-positive rate bounded during repeated looks.
Fallback metrics: for low-sample cohorts use signed effect-size thresholds (Cohen's d) with Bayesian posterior intervals to decide conservatively.
Time windows: sliding windows of 5 minutes with configurable aggregation (counts, medians, quantiles). Consecutive-window requirement default=3 for rollback pacing.
Risk budget: each rollout has a budget (initial default 0.05 alpha) and controller reduces budget on each marginally significant hit; rollbacks happen only when burn-rate indicates urgent action.
Cohorting: tenant_id, request_route, and model_variant form cohort key. Support custom cohort labels supplied by customer in rollout config.

Control plane actions: controller calls rollout-controller API with action payload {type: 'rollback', reason: 'quality_regression', metadata: {...}}. Rollback flow must attach eval snapshot id and PR/commit references for traceability.
Observability: push metrics to Prometheus and Graphite (latency: 1s buckets, token-quality: 30s buckets). Console shows per-metric heatmap and a timeline of decisions.
Security: audit events written to KMS-encrypted log stream for Private deployments; no sensitive content in logs (only IDs and metric deltas).
Operational safety: include manual pause and dry-run modes. Dry-run writes decisions to logs and emits alerts but does not change routing.
Performance note: heavy evals (per-request human-labeled checks) are sampled at 1% by default and routed to off-path evaluation pipeline to avoid control-plane load spikes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy metrics cause unnecessary rollbacks - Mitigation: sequential tests + min-sample guards + risk budget
Risk: automatic rollback could violate enterprise change controls in Private deployments - Mitigation: opt-in auto-rollback for Private; default to alert-only unless customer allows automation
Risk: rollback causes oscillation between two versions - Mitigation: cooldown period after rollback (configurable, default 30 minutes) and exponential backoff for retries
Risk: high-cardinality cohorts increase memory/compute - Mitigation: TTL and heavy-hitter retention, aggregate low-volume cohorts into an "other" bucket
deployment_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag behind server-side config; dry-run only in staging for 2 weeks; collect false-positive rate metrics
Phase 2: Enable in hosted for internal customers with 1% of rollouts, require manual approval for Dedicated/Private; monitor for 1 week
Phase 3: Gradually increase traffic coverage to 25% for hosted; enable opt-in auto-rollback for Dedicated after security review
Phase 4: GA with Console controls (risk budget, min-sample, cohorts) and docs for customers
